gloss: to sit in seiza; to sit formally on one's knees

definitions.gloss: to sit in seiza; to sit formally on one's knees
definitions.explanation: To sit in the traditional Japanese kneeling position with legs folded underneath, back straight, and hands resting on the thighs. The formal sitting posture used in tea ceremony, martial arts, and formal occasions.

examples.japanese: {畳|たたみ}の{上|うえ}で{正座|せいざ}する。
examples.english: To sit in seiza on the tatami.

examples.japanese: {長|なが}い{時間|じかん}{正座|せいざ}していたので、{足|あし}がしびれた。
examples.english: My legs went numb because I was sitting in seiza for a long time.

examples.japanese: {茶道|さどう}では、お{茶|ちゃ}をいただくときに{正座|せいざ}するのが{基本|きほん}だ。
examples.english: In tea ceremony, sitting in seiza when receiving tea is the basic etiquette.

notes:
The standard formal sitting position in Japanese culture, where one kneels with the tops of the feet flat on the floor and sits back on the heels. It is expected in traditional settings such as tea ceremony, martial arts practice, and Buddhist rituals.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {正座|せいざ}をする: to sit in seiza (with を particle)
- {正座|せいざ}で{座|すわ}る: to sit in seiza position
- {正座|せいざ}がつらい: seiza is uncomfortable
- {足|あし}がしびれる: legs go numb (from sitting in seiza)

CULTURAL NOTE:
While traditionally the expected sitting posture on tatami, younger generations of Japanese people are increasingly unaccustomed to sitting in seiza for extended periods. In modern casual settings, あぐらをかく (sitting cross-legged) is often permitted, especially for men. Women may sit with legs to one side ({横座|よこずわ}り).

SIMILAR WORDS:
- あぐらをかく: to sit cross-legged — the casual alternative to {正座|せいざ}, considered less formal
- {膝|ひざ}をつく: to kneel (on one or both knees) — different posture from {正座|せいざ}, which involves sitting back on the heels
